components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main call-to-action button, used sparingly per the One Voice Rule.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #E63946; color: #fff; padding: 16px 48px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 4px; transition: background 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.9); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #00BFFF; outline-offset: 2px; background: #E63946; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { border: 1px solid #070A40; color: #070A40; padding: 16px 48px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 500; background: transparent; border-radius: 4px; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(7, 10, 64, 0.05); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #00BFFF; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.css: .ds-nav-link { color: #00BFFF; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.2s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: #E63946; }

narrative.overview: LightSpeed Holdings is the AI-native company builder for Southern Africa. The visual system reflects institutional credibility with a disciplined, geometry-first aesthetic: navy as the anchoring authority, cyan as the trust signal, and red as the accent that demands attention. The design language treats the web as a set of editorial pages — structured, scannable, and grounded in hierarchy. Every element either serves the content or recedes.
keyCharacteristics: Governance-visible: the approval matrix, lifecycle, and honesty badges are not decoration — they are the product
Typographic rhythm: Arial as the single system font, with a clear display-to-body scale
Navy-first colour strategy: the primary accent is rare by design, making its appearance meaningful
Mobile-first spacing: the 4px grid resolves to compact mobile units before expanding to desktop rhythm
Transparency in evidence: the four-level honesty badge system is surface-visible, not hidden

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The primary accent (navy `#070A40`) is used on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Cyan-Is-Trust Rule
rules.body: Cyan `#00BFFF` is the sole trust signal. It replaces green in all status, success, and error contexts.

rules.name: The Arial-Only Rule
rules.body: No custom web fonts are loaded. Arial is the single typeface family across all surfaces and modes.

dos: Use navy `#070A40` as the primary accent, keeping it ≤10% of any screen surface
Use cyan `#00BFFF` as the trust signal — on focus rings, link colours, and success states
Use red `#E63946` as the CTA accent; use it sparingly
Honesty badge colours exactly as specified — do not substitute or remix
Arial as the single typeface family across all themes and surfaces
4px corner radius on buttons, inputs, cards, and containers
16px base unit / 4px scale for all spacing
Vertical section rhythm of 64px on desktop, 48px on mobile
The cyan focus-visible ring (3px, 2px offset) on every focusable element
Honour prefers-reduced-motion by collapsing all animation/transition durations to 0.01ms
donts: Use green for status or success — cyan is the trust signal, not green
Invent additional colour roles beyond primary/accent/trust/neutral
Apply custom web fonts; Arial only
Use border-radius: 0 on interactive components (buttons, inputs, cards)
Add decorative drop shadows beyond the specified elevation tokens
Layer more than one primary accent colour on a single surface
Skip the skip link or focus-visible ring on the marketing site
